source: Derived from NASA data: warning = 95th percentile of heart rate (1,546 windows, 17 subjects, NASA Crew State Monitoring dataset). Danger = NASA OCHMO-STD-100.1A Appendix A, G.8.A.i(5) p.76 (above 130 at rest) and G.8.C.i(8) p.77 (below 30) (astronaut medical selection standard)

Warning = NASA OCHMO-STD-100.1A Appendix A, G.3, p.75: sustained systolic 140 mmHg or higher (astronaut medical selection standard). Danger = US government reference: NIH NHLBI, hypertensive crisis higher than 180 systolic

Warning = NASA OCHMO-STD-100.1A Appendix A, G.3, p.75: sustained diastolic 90 mmHg or higher (astronaut medical selection standard). Danger = US government reference: NIH NHLBI, hypertensive crisis higher than 120 diastolic
US government reference: NIH MedlinePlus, Pulse Oximetry: contact a provider at 92% or lower (warning, whole-number readings) and seek immediate attention at 88% or lower (danger)
US government reference: NIH NIDDK, Low Blood Glucose: a reading lower than 70 mg/dL is low
US government reference: NIH MedlinePlus, Fever: an adult probably has a fever above 37.2 to 37.5 C by mouth (warning); contact a provider right away if it stays above 39.4 C (danger)
NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C, V1 4027 (sec 4.7.2, p. 39): hip and spine at or above 95% of pre-mission value
NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C, V1 4030 (sec 4.8.2, p. 40): career effective dose less than 600 mSv. Reference only (not an alarm): V1 4031 design solar particle event less than 250 mSv
